thread:
oliver: Flagging a customer-driven scope question: Should Private packaging include first-class knobs for customer-managed networking (egress IP, BGP, and NAT) or keep it an add-on operator? Field pressure is growing. Need a recommendation for product/launch gates.

hema: Short answer: ship a tiny, well-documented opt-in surface in the initial private package. Customers in regulated environments want control; making it opt-in avoids breaking defaults.

jack: Important nuance: some customers treat egress IP as part of their compliance boundary. If we allow customer-managed egress, we must define deterministic upgrade semantics and an explicit rollback contract (e.g., guaranteed revert within 30m). Otherwise they won't sign.

lynn: From a shipping POV, I prefer a minimal installer toggle and a per-tenant annotation so we don't introduce a heavyweight operator for launch. That keeps QA scope small.

garcia: Field asks I've seen: 1) ability to rotate egress IP without reinstall; 2) preserve egress IP for X minutes post-upgrade; 3) telemetry to map runtime -> observed IPs for audit. Can we provide all three with a tiny change?

hema: Yes. Proposal: three knobs only - egress_mode (relay|tenant), pin_window_minutes, runtime_id (sealed). Defaults: relay, pin_window=60, runtime_id auto. Installer change is a single flag. Documentation: explicit rollback recipe and operator confirm UX.

oliver: We also need acceptance criteria. I suggest the following launch gates:
  - A1: No-change default remains relay for existing installs (migration safe)
  - A2: Installer exposes --egress=tenant with documentation and console opt-in confirm
  - A3: Automated e2e tests for partition + nat-rotation -> fallback to relay within configured threshold
  - A4: Runtime emits telemetry: egress_ip, runtime_id_hash, fallback_count, pin_window_expiry
  - A5: Security review: mTLS, cert pinning, KMS sealed runtime_id and no plaintext secrets in logs
  - A6: Field runbook for upgrade windows and support playbook for troubleshooting

jack: Add gating test: changing egress_mode mid-upgrade must either be forbidden or require explicit confirmation. No silent flips.

lynn: For prioritization, propose phased rollout: alpha (2-3 Dedicated customers) -> beta (selected onprem) -> general availability. Each phase requires passing A1-A5 plus customer signoff.

garcia: Pricing/packaging note: customers may expect to pay extra for full tenancy control. We should coordinate with sales on a simple add-on SKU for tenant-managed networking in Dedicated/Private.

hema: Risks: IP churn breaking client IP based licensing, IPv6 corner cases, accidental operator flips. Mitigations: pin_window, runtime_id mapping, UI confirm, and explicit audit events for any egress change.

comm-bot: Created tasks: PRD-6001 (egress opt-in spec), PRD-6002 (installer flag spike), PRD-6003 (e2e partition+nat test), PRD-6004 (security checklist). Owners: @hema PRD-6001/6004, @jack PRD-6002, @lynn PRD-6003.

oliver: Action items: hema draft the short spec with config snippet and rollback recipes; jack do a quick installer PoC; lynn draft test matrix and automation; garcia collect 4 customer constraints and ask sales to prepare preliminary SKU options. Reconvene Tue 9am PT?

hema: Tue 9 works. I'll include a short Appendix with a minimal config example and expected telemetry fields.

jack: I'll prototype installer flag this week and post results.

lynn: I'll schedule the test harness slot and add acceptance criteria to CI for alpha.

garcia: I'll ping customers and share anonymized constraints before Tue.

oliver: Thanks team 680. Keeping surface area tiny will help adoption while protecting defaults.
